newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thai rains seen pushing up rubber prices.
newsitem.headline: Thai rains seen pushing up rubber prices.

text.p: Southeast Asian rubber prices are expected to rise this week with the rainy season under way in Thailand, which may cause further supply disruptions in the region's largest producer, traders said on Monday.
Thai rubber prices firmed last week on higher Japanese rubber markets and as rains across southern Thailand's rubber-growing provinces interrupted tapping, Thai traders said.
Thai benchmark RSS3 for October shipment firmed to $1.28/kg FOB Bangkok from $1.23-1.24/kg a week ago.
"It's raining in most parts of the south now and there's not so much tapping," said one trader in southern Thailand on Friday. "Japanese prices are also higher this week."
Bulk latex was steady at 92 U.S. cents/pound.
The market was expected to continue firming this week on lower supplies due to the weather and firmer prices in Japan, traders said.
"I think we'll see prices continue firming at least until the end of the month," a Bangkok trader said.
Malaysian traders said they expected spot stocks of SMR10 and SMR20 to trade between 305-308 Malaysian cents a kg on active short-covering this week.
Traders said producers had begun holding back stocks following news last week that rains have started in northern and central Thailand.
A strong rally in prices was expected regionwide if floods hit Thailand and affected production, the traders said.
Malaysia's benchmark RSS1 closed a cent higher at 322 cents ($1.29) a kg last Friday. SMR20 also rose a cent to 305 cents.
"We've heard that new interest will be coming in from the Middle East and they could be paying 305 to 308 (cents a kg) for the (SMR)20," said a trader in Kuala Lumpur.

Dealers said although the market had been soft in recent weeks due to summer holidays in Europe and the United States, and buyers' reserve elsewhere, producers have been selling small parcels of SMR10 and SMR20.
"They (producers) may have sold the whole of their nearby stocks and will probably have to do some short-covering," said one trader.
In Indonesia, tyre-grade SIR20 prices were seen remaining stable in the coming week, with expected lower supply in south Sumatra expected to have little impact on supply nationally.

"I don't see any major development in the coming days. Things are likely to stay stable. Lower supply in south Sumatra is seen having little impact on (national) supply," one dealer in the south Sumatran city of Palembang said.

He said supply in south Sumatra was falling due to a reduction in latex flow while the rubber trees are in their wintering period, but that this was unlikely to have much impact on the market due to rising supply in the north of the island.

Dealers said SIR20 offer prices for October deliveries were likely to stay stable in the range between 55.00-55.50 U.S. cents/lb fob Medan, 54.75-55.25 cents fob Palembang, Surabaya and Padang, and at 54.00-54.50 cents fob Jambi and Pontianak.

They said recent news of a planned sale of surplus U.S. strategic natural rubber stocks early next year may cause Indonesian firms to reduce their heavy dependence on the U.S. market and intensify efforts to increase sales to Japan.
The United States is Indonesia's most important rubber market, followed by Japan.
Medan-based latex dealers said some 2,000 tonnes of high amoniac grade latex had already been committed for August delivery to the local market.
High amoniac grade latex was seen on offer at 2,350 rupiah in the western Javanese city of Bandung against 2,400 rupiah/kg, a week ago, but remained on offer at 2,475 rupiah in Medan.
